title: Dependency Chateau and Rollout Slicing Walkthrough
summary: Walkthrough of the new dependency isolation pattern ("chateau") and rollout slicing plan for the upcoming inference launch. Covered canary sizing, eviction behavior, fallback routing, and runbook handoff. Agreed on immediate action items: finalize slice definitions, run a 10% strain sim, and author the chateau dependency map.
topics: fallback routing and model variant mapping
next_steps: Priya to finalize slice definitions and post to #launch-readiness by 2027-04-18
Marco to run 10% strain sim and share results in the benchmarking doc by 2027-04-20
Elaine to update eviction telemetry and set alerts before the next canary
Noor to schedule staged canary windows and coordinate with infra for reserve capacity
Samir to run a quick SOC checklist on the chateau design and flag gaps
action_items: Priya Kapoor: publish slice matrix and success criteria - due 2027-04-18
Marco Alvarez: run strain simulation (10%) and capture latency/cost tradeoffs - due 2027-04-20

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-14 15:00 PDT
Duration: 78 minutes
Attendees: Priya, Marco, Elaine, Noor, Samir, Jordan

AUTO-SUMMARY:
Priya: quick walkthrough of the chateau pattern and the rollout slices, want to make sure the oncall runbook is aligned and the canary windows are gated by both latency and error budgets.

[00:00] Priya: okay folks, thanks for joining, we have 78 minutes, let's try to keep to the agenda. main goal is to lock the slice definitions and hand off the runbook.
[00:28] Marco: yeah, I put up the dependency map, sorry I call it the chateau to be less verbosy, it's basically layered isolation, ring one is critical libs, ring two is optional quantized paths, ring three is heuristics and caching.
[00:53] Elaine: can you repeat ring two? I think the notes earlier said qpath, qpath could be quantized kernels or half precision. sometimes the auto-quant path gets swapped for a fallback and that changes memory.
[01:20] Marco: right, so ring two is quantized/fast kernels. ring one is native fp16 kernels, ring three is the cache-heavy helpers. the reason we want a chateau is to be able to evict outer rings under memory pressure while keeping the hot path intact.
[01:46] Noor: for rollout slicing we need to map users to slices, my thought is not purely percent-based. we should slice by request-profile buckets — short-chat, long-context, and embeddings heavy. then do staggered percents across them.
[02:13] Samir: and add a security gating: any slice touching PII flagged flows must go through HSM/KMS check. we need a simple yes/no in the slice matrix.
[02:37] Priya: agreed. quick poll: are we comfortable with three slices? short-chat (50%), long-context (30%), embeddings (20%) as starting point?
[02:58] Jordan: small note, the 50% for short-chat should probably be 40% if we want to be conservative on the first canary, also depends on whether we run at peak or off-peak.
[03:23] Elaine: can we run a 10% strain sim on production-ish images to see eviction churn first? that should tell us if the chateau evictions are working as designed.
[03:48] Marco: yes I'll do that. Marco: side note, our eviction policy still has that bug where the KV cache isn't always counted towards the slab, so eviction order can be off. I have a patch but haven't landed it.
[04:10] Priya: that patch needs to get in before the canary. can we commit to the patch by next week?
[04:22] Marco: I can try to land it by Thursday. low risk, needs e2e perf check.
[04:37] Noor: for canary windows, I'd prefer three windows over two: 10% initial, then 30%, then the 40-50% depending on signals. That aligns with Priya but gives us a safety net.
[05:00] Priya: okay, so timeline suggestion: slice defs by Monday, patch and 10% sim mid-week, initial canary the following week.
[05:20] Samir: also, I want us to define what 'failure' means operationally for the canary: 95th percentile latency above baseline + error rate > X% + any data exfil alerts. we should keep it simple.
[05:45] Elaine: agree, specifically 95th latency + p99 for long contexts, because for long-context requests p99 is the real user impact.
[06:03] Jordan: can we add a token-cost signal? sometimes a small latency blip has huge cost implications if the token accounting goes up.
[06:18] Marco: good call. we'll add token-per-request as a metric.
[06:29] Priya: moving on — fallback routing. if ring two evicts, we should route to a compatible model variant, maybe a size-up or quant-down? Thoughts?
[06:46] Marco: compatible variant mapping table: if quantized kernel fails, map to fp16 but with a stricter max-steps cap. If fp16 fails, route to a smaller model variant with best-effort decoding. This will increase cost but keep availability.
[07:10] Noor: we need to ensure the routing code honors request-level hints — customer may prefer cost over latency. we'll need a header for preference.
[07:25] Samir: and for compliance we must ensure fallback doesn't route to regions outside allowed residency. add a region guard.
[07:40] Priya: copy. next — runbook handoff. Elaine, can you outline oncall steps for an eviction storm?
[07:52] Elaine: step one: triage alert triggers (eviction rate > threshold), step two: identify affected chateau ring, step three: force-evict outer ring if automated policy fails, step four: trigger fallback routing to smaller variant, step five: engage release to scale burst capacity.
[08:20] Noor: on the scaling callouts, I'd like a pre-authorized short burst reservation so we can scale without manual approval, else rollout stalls. we should bake that into the canary config.
[08:38] Marco: pre-authorized capacity is fine, but we need cost guardrails. maybe an auto-scale cap at 2x baseline and automatic downgrade of non-critical slices if we hit twice baseline.
[08:58] Priya: okay let's mark that as a requirement.
[09:10] [09:10] Marco: (mumbles) one more perf caveat — kernel fallback adds jitter; we should expect a transient p95 spike when a node starts using fallback kernels. that's expected but must be within SLO.
[09:32] Samir: question — do we need an external audit before launch? I think a lightweight SOC-style review is enough, full audit not necessary for initial canary but required before GA.
[09:53] Priya: lightweight review pre-canary, full audit pre-GA — agreed. Samir, you own the lightweight one.
[10:05] Samir: noted.
[10:12] Jordan: quick note about comms: marketing wants a two-line blurb for release notes but we should not promise latency numbers until GA.
[10:25] Priya: good point. keep public comms minimal.
[10:32] [10:32] Marco: starting to run the 10% strain sim will help with comms too, gives us numbers to show engineering confidence.
[10:50] Elaine: telemetry gaps — we don't currently surface per-slice token-cost, only per-model. we'll need a small tagging change in the ingress to surface slice tag.
[11:07] Noor: I can schedule a small change window for ingress tagging, but that will require coordination with ingress owners; might be 24-48 hours to land.
[11:23] Priya: let's add that to the action items.
[11:33] [11:33] Marco: question about rollback criteria: is a rollback automatic or manual? I propose automatic rollback if token cost exceeds 2x or error rate > X for more than 5 minutes.
[11:54] Elaine: auto rollback could be dangerous if a monitoring flap causes repeated rollbacks. maybe auto rollback only if multiple signals align and a cooldown.
[12:12] Priya: we'll do a conservative auto-rollback: need 3 signals (latency, error, token-cost) for 2 consecutive minutes before an auto-rollback. otherwise manual.
[12:34] Samir: log retention — for canary scope we keep detailed logs for 30 days; for full GA it's 90 days. need to make sure storage costs are accounted for.
[12:52] Noor: noted. I'll model storage delta in the canary cost spreadsheet.
[13:05] [13:05] Marco: ok I'm going to run the patch for KV accounting and then the strain sim. timeline wise it looks doable.
[13:18] Priya: one more sticky point — the chateau mapping needs a clear owner in the codebase. who's owning the mapping and the enforcement? Marco: infra or runtime?
[13:35] Marco: my team will own enforcement in runtime, but infra will own the eviction knobs and observable surface.
[13:48] Elaine: we should create a small RFC for chateau enforcement boundaries so it's not tribal knowledge.
[13:59] Priya: yes please. Marco to write RFC draft, Elaine to own telemetry requirements section, Noor to own rollout knobs.
[14:12] Jordan: notable question from Jeff in #launch-readiness — how do we surface the user preference header when customers use the SDKs? is there an SDK change required?
[14:30] Marco: minimal SDK change: add optional header flag that is passed through. backward compatible. we'll add to SDK backlog.
[14:45] Priya: Great. At this point let's open the floor for risks and objections.
[14:55] Elaine: risk — eviction thrash if we mis-tune the slab thresholds. mitigation: do small incremental adjustments with offline sim before canary.
[15:10] Samir: risk — fallback could route to variants that don't meet compliance; mitigation — region guard and policy map.
[15:25] Noor: ops risk — if ingress tagging fails we'll lose slice visibility; mitigation — fallback to model-level telemetry and increase retention window for debugging.
[15:40] Marco: dev risk — landing kernel accounting patch could have perf ripple; mitigation: smoke tests + canary node pool.
[15:58] Priya: all good, let's capture these on the risk register.
[16:10] [16:10] Jordan: quick recap — slice defs, kernel patch, 10% sim, ingress tagging, pre-authorized burst capacity, lightweight security preflight. Anything else?
[16:30] Samir: add runbook steps and contact list for oncall.
[16:38] Priya: ok, next meeting cadence — twice weekly until initial canary closes.
[16:47] Noor: I'll schedule them.
[16:55] Marco: I'll post the strain sim plan in the benchmarking doc and tag everyone.
[17:05] Priya: thanks all. end of main agenda.

AUTO-ACTION-ITEMS (verbatim):
- Priya: publish slice matrix and success criteria - due 2027-04-18
- Marco: run strain simulation (10%) and capture latency/cost tradeoffs - due 2027-04-20
- Elaine: add eviction heatmap to dashboards + configure alert thresholds - due 2027-04-19
- Noor: reserve 2x burst capacity for canary windows + schedule canary - due 2027-04-22
- Samir: security preflight checklist for dependency chateau - due 2027-04-21

[58:12] Priya: quick check — anyone have additional blockers?
[58:30] Marco: nothing else from infra.
[58:38] Elaine: no.
[58:45] Noor: no.
[58:50] Samir: nope.
[58:55] Jordan: I'll capture notes and update Confluence.
[59:05] Priya: great, meeting adjourned.

End transcript.
